tasks.title: Test the engine probe with Gemini and Antigravity profile shapes
tasks.goal: Create test/engine-probe.test.mjs using node:test. Import probeEngine, profileFlags and resolveProfile from ../.harness/lib/common.mjs. Set process.env.HARNESS_ROOT to a fresh temp directory BEFORE importing so the probe cache never touches the repo, and put fake executable shell scripts on PATH. Cases: (1) fake 'gemini' whose --help lists '-y, --yolo' -> compatible, auto picks gemini when it is first in autoOrder; (2) fake 'antigravity' with VS Code style help (no --headless/--json) -> compatible=false, missing lists both flags, resolveProfile('antigravity') falls back with fallbackFrom='antigravity'; (3) no gemini or antigravity on PATH -> installed=false; (4) help text that prints nothing -> checked=false and treated as compatible. Build the config object inline from .harness/config.json profiles (read the JSON). Do not edit anything under .harness/. Use only the Node standard library. ALSO (approved by the human): in test/run-tests.mjs change ONLY the helper sandbox(): keep every static .harness/ config and template file in the sandbox copy, but reset the copied .harness/backlog.json to the clean empty shipped state {"version":"2.0.0","project":"","maxAutoTasksPerRun":3,"tasks":[]} and exclude or remove the copied active run state (.harness/visible/), so npm test passes while a real harness run is open. Do not change any test case, other helper, package.json or anything under .harness/.

tasks.title: Write docs/ENGINES.md: running Gemini and Antigravity with a subscription
tasks.goal: Create docs/ENGINES.md for a developer who uses Gemini and Antigravity and a subscription-only, no-API-key policy. Sections: which engines exist and how autoOrder picks one (first installed engine whose flags pass '<binary> --help'); log in with the subscription (Gemini: run 'gemini' and choose Login with Google; no GEMINI_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment); check with 'node .harness/doctor.mjs'; what ENGINE_FALLBACK in .harness/telemetry.log means; cloud sessions cannot do browser login so they use Claude Code; engine profiles in config.json are marked verified false until a real run succeeds. Only mention scripts and paths that exist in this repo. Plain English, short. Do not edit anything under .harness/.
